Question B-006-011-009.

Why the correct answer is right: Increasing the element diameter lowers the element Q and makes the antenna less sharply tuned, so the Yagi keeps an acceptable match over a wider frequency range.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Decrease the element spacing": Closer spacing changes coupling and can reduce performance; it is not the standard way to broaden a Yagi bandwidth.
- sourceIndex 2: "Install loading coils in the elements": Loading coils add reactance and loss and usually make an antenna more sharply tuned, so they tend to narrow rather than widen bandwidth.
- sourceIndex 3: "Use tapered elements": Tapering is mainly a mechanical construction choice. The bandwidth principle being tested is larger effective element diameter.
